content: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases lopinavir levels or effects by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme involved in hepatic and intestinal metabolism. Similarly, lopinavir increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels or effects through the same mechanism. These drugs should be avoided or replaced with alternatives. Erythromycin lactobionate also increases lopinavir levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and lopinavir reciprocally increases erythromycin lactobionate levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Erythromycin stearate interacts similarly, increasing lopinavir levels or effects via CYP3A4 inhibition, and lopinavir increases erythromycin stearate levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Escitalopram increases lopinavir toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Lopinavir affects ethinyl estradiol levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially causing significant changes in estrogen plasma levels and reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Non-hormonal contraceptives are recommended. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases everolimus levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Lopinavir increases fedratinib levels or effects via CYP3A4 inhibition. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the fedratinib dose to 200 mg/day. If the CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued, gradually increase the fedratinib dose as tolerated. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases felbamate levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases fentanyl levels or effects (including intranasal, transdermal, and transmucosal forms) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is necessary, monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust fentanyl doses as needed. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir decreases fexinidazole levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4, increasing the risk of adverse effects with CYP3A4 substrates. Fingolimod and lopinavir both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases intranasal fluticasone levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, which may lead to systemic corticosteroid adverse effects such as Cushing syndrome. Monitor for signs of high corticosteroid concentrations. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases fosamprenavir levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Gemifloxacin and lopinavir both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases gilteritinib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor closely for gilteritinib-related adverse effects. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Lopinavir and givinostat both prolong the QTc interval. If coadministration is unavoidable, obtain ECGs during initiation and treatment, and withhold treatment if the QTc interval exceeds 500 ms or increases by more than 60 ms from baseline. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases glasdegib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for QTc prolongation. Lopinavir increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels or effects by decreasing metabolism. Avoid coadministration with lopinavir, as it is a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. Granisetron and lopinavir both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases haloperidol levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Histrelin increases lopinavir toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and lopinavir both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases hydroxyprogesterone caproate levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Hydroxyzine and lopinavir both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases ibrutinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concomitant use with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If short-term use of a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is necessary, interrupt ibrutinib therapy until the inhibitor is discontinued. Lopinavir increases idelalisib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministered, monitor for idelalisib toxicity and adjust dosage as needed. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases imatinib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases infigratinib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Inotuzumab and lopinavir both prolong the QTc interval. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor ECGs and electrolytes before and during treatment. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Isoflurane and lopinavir both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases isradipine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases itraconazole levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases ivosidenib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the ivosidenib dose to 250 mg daily. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases ixabepilone levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases lapatinib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases larotrectinib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the larotrectinib dose by 50%. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases lefamulin levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Lopinavir increases lemborexant levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Lopinavir increases leniolisib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir affects levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate levels, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Use nonhormonal contraceptives. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lithium and lopinavir both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases lorlatinib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the lorlatinib dose by 25 mg daily. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases lurasidone levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Lopinavir increases lurbinectedin levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the lurbinectedin dose by 50%. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Macimorelin and lopinavir both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration with drugs that prolong the QT interval, as this increases the risk of torsades de pointes. Lopinavir also increases macimorelin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases macitentan levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Lopinavir increases mefloquine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Mefloquine also enhances QTc prolongation. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases mestranol levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases metaxalone levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases methadone levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases methylprednisolone levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases midazolam levels or effects (including intranasal forms) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially prolonging sedation. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases midostaurin levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for adverse reactions, especially during the first week of treatment. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Mirtazapine and lopinavir both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases nelfinavir levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases neratinib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Lopinavir increases nevirapine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases nicardipine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases nilotinib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases nirogacestat levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Olanzapine and lopinavir both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases olaparib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the olaparib dose to 150 mg (capsule) or 100 mg (tablet) twice daily. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases omaveloxolone levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 50 mg daily and monitor closely for adverse effects. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases paritaprevir levels when coadministered with ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir. This combination is not recommended. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases ondansetron levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases osimertinib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If unavoidable, monitor closely for adverse effects. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Oxaliplatin and lopinavir both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases oxycodone levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction may be warranted. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases paclitaxel levels or effects (including protein-bound forms) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases palbociclib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the palbociclib dose to 75 mg daily. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases palovarotene levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir and panobinostat both prolong the QTc interval. Panobinostat significantly prolongs the QT interval, and its use with QT-prolonging drugs is not recommended. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases pazopanib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases pexidartinib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose as per the drug monograph. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases pimavanserin levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of cardiac arrhythmia. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases pimozide levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Lopinavir increases pirtobrutinib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the pirtobrutinib dose by 50 mg. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir and pitolisant both prolong the QTc interval. Lopinavir also increases pitolisant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases pomalidomide levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporters. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases ponatinib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the ponatinib starting dose to 30 mg daily. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases pralsetinib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Primaquine and lopinavir both prolong the QTc interval. Lopinavir increases romidepsin levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases rosuvastatin levels by decreasing metabolism. Limit the rosuvastatin dose to 10 mg daily. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases ruxolitinib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the starting dose to 10 mg twice daily if platelet counts are ≥100 x 10^9/L. Avoid use with platelet counts <100 x 10^9/L. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Avoid or use alternative drugs.
